chapter: Harlem musicians and the road with Armstrong
title: Touring by bus and Armstrong's red Packard
summary: The band toured everywhere by bus with Armstrong's dogs, wife Alpha and a maid, while Armstrong refused to ride in Glaser's red Packard that Holmes rode in instead.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: All over the country. All over the South. All over the South. All over the West. The Midwest. The Far West. The Northwest. The Northeast. All over. Everywhere in the country.
Bus. We had our own bus. We had a nice bus. There was nothing wrong with the bus.
Everybody was in one big bus.
Yup, one big one. Everybody was there. I think Louis had two...two Boston Bulldogs -- they was in there, too.

Alpha. Oh boy, it was somethin' when they come in the bus, with the two dogs and one thing and another. I think they had a maid, too. He had a maid and a chauffeur -- Louis had a chauffeur. Because Joe Glaser bought a big red Packard, a beautiful car, and had this chauffeur to drive for Louis, and he'd go on the road with Louis. Louis wouldn't ride in the car. He wouldn't ride in the car, I don't know why. He got in the bus; he piled up in the bus.

Now, that don't make too much sense to me, because if you... Say, like, you're leavin' anywhere... Say we're leavin' here and we're going to Washington. Well now, with a bus, it'll take four hours to get down to Washington. Well, in a car, you could at least save an hour -- at least an hour; maybe even more time than that. And they could get in the room or wherever you've got to go, and stretch out and get that much more rest.

With a bus, you've got a bus full of people, and they always have to be makin' stops for this-that-or-the-other, and you can lose a lot of time in a bus. And Louis wouldn't ride in a bus. He'd be with his band, his show, his people. So what happened to the bus...?

To the car. Bob Smiley had to drive the car, and Sonny Moore, vocalist, and myself, we rode the car with Smiley. We rode with him. I wasn't too ashamed to ride with him -- a great, big, beautiful red Packard. And brother, when we ride into any of them towns, well, you thought we were somethin'. And we'd get there ahead of time. We could get to the hotel and get rooms -- there's no trouble gettin' rooms. We'd be the first one in town, get our rooms -- and when they comin' down, we'd be in bed sleeping.

Oh, brother. We were somethin', this big red Packard would drive into town, and who would step out but little-bitty me and Sonny Moore -- Sonny was no taller than me. But Louis wouldn't ride in it; he wouldn't ride in that car. And I told him, I said, "I don't blame you."
